name: Tirion Fordring
summary: Beside the Thondroril River, Tirion Fordring watches Lordaeron's tragedy unfold from exile. Once a paladin and lord of Mardenholde Keep, he lost his title and lands for honoring an oath to an enemy orc. Now he worries for his son.

sections.title: A Knight of the Silver Hand
sections.body: Before Lordaeron fell, Tirion Fordring was among its finest knights. He served as a paladin of the Knights of the Silver Hand, founded by Archbishop Alonsus Faol during the Second War. With plate, hammer, and faith in the Holy Light, he fought the Old Horde. His fellow knights revered him as a steadfast example of the Light's power.

sections.title: A Matter of Honor and Exile
sections.body:
After the Second War, Tirion governed Hearthglen from Mardenholde Keep with his wife Karandra and their young son Taelan. Then he met Eitrigg, an aged orc warrior living as a hermit, and saw honor in him. Tirion promised to protect Eitrigg.

When Alliance authorities found the orc, Tirion fought his own countrymen to keep that oath. The Alliance of Lordaeron stripped Tirion of his nobility, and the Silver Hand cast him out. He was banished, while Uther spared Karandra and Taelan from the sentence.

sections.title: A Father's Torment
sections.body: After Tirion's exile, Taelan remained in Hearthglen with his mother. Lordaeron fell to the Scourge during the Third War, and Taelan grew to manhood and joined the Scarlet Crusade. In time, he became Hearthglen's Highlord. From afar, Tirion watches the Crusade descend into madness. He grieves that fanaticism has made his son its puppet. Memories of happier days, including family visits to Caer Darrow, keep Tirion searching for a way to remind Taelan of true honor.

faq.answer: Tirion Fordring once governed Hearthglen and served as a paladin of the Knights of the Silver Hand. His peers exiled him for defending an orc out of honor. He now lives in a cabin on the western edge of the Eastern Plaguelands.

faq.q: Why was Tirion exiled from Lordaeron?
faq.answer: Tirion met Eitrigg, an aged orc veteran, and recognized his sense of honor. When Alliance forces found Eitrigg, Tirion fought his own comrades to keep his promise to protect him. The Alliance stripped Tirion of his titles and banished him from the kingdom.

faq.q: What is Tirion's connection to Hearthglen?
faq.answer: Hearthglen was Tirion's seat, and he governed it from Mardenholde Keep until his exile. His son, Highlord Taelan Fordring, commands the Scarlet Crusade there.

faq.q: Does Tirion still have his paladin powers?
faq.answer: The Church and the Silver Hand stripped Tirion of his rank and claimed to revoke his holy powers. Yet his conviction kept his bond with the Holy Light unbroken. The Light still answers his will as strongly as ever.

faq.q: What does Tirion want with the Scarlet Crusade?
aliases: why does tirion care about the crusade
faq.answer: Tirion wants to reach his son Taelan, a high commander of the Scarlet Crusade in Hearthglen. He hopes to awaken Taelan's conscience and free him from the Crusade's corruption before his soul is lost.

faq.q: Who are the other original paladins?
faq.answer: Archbishop Alonsus Faol founded the Knights of the Silver Hand during the Second War, with Uther the Lightbringer as its first paladin. Tirion's fellow knights included Turalyon and his close friend Saidan Dathrohan.

angles.text: As a paladin, you stand before a knight of the Silver Hand from the Second War. He mastered the Holy Light and honored an oath above mortal law.
As a human, you meet a hero of the Alliance of Lordaeron who ruled Hearthglen justly. He recalls the noble kingdom that fell into rot and madness.
As an orc, you meet a former enemy who slew many in the Second War. He surrendered his land, family, and name rather than break an oath of honor to Eitrigg.
As an Alliance member, you meet a man who held to the Alliance's ideals. Its kingdoms branded him a traitor for placing personal honor above racial hatred.
